title: Digitization of the AWMF guideline registry for an open, guideline-based, trustworthy evidence ecosystem - a before-after study with different user groups
summary:
Guidelines are essential for medical care. The aim of the Dissolve-E project is to make trustworthy guideline knowledge available in the long term and easier to use in various treatment contexts. To this end, the AWMF's previously analog guideline register will be digitally implemented. The project partners are developing a digital infrastructure and technical standards for data exchange that comply with international standards. In addition, the researchers are developing instructions to enable users to get started easily with the digital creation of guidelines; this also includes methodological support options. Existing guidelines will then be transferred to the digital register.
The development and introduction of the digital register will then be evaluated. Surveys and focus groups will be conducted for this purpose. In particular, the usability, acceptance and trustworthiness of the digital register and its content will be assessed. In this way, further opportunities for improvement can be found.

Various user groups are included for this purpose. These include: 
1. guideline authors, 
2. guideline administrators from scientific medical societies, 
3. users of the AWMF guideline register:
i) Registry users (healthcare professionals as well as patients and employees of healthcare institutions)
ii) Guideline users at the ‘point of care’ in outpatient settings (clinicians working in outpatient settings and patients - this is specifically about the display of guideline recommendations on doctors' screens or in layperson-friendly language for patients). 
iii) Guideline users at the inpatient point of care (senior physicians in intensive care units - here too, the focus is on displaying guideline recommendations on doctors' screens and their usability). 
4. technical guideline users (API users).

This study is a before-and-after intervention study on medical knowledge management and has a direct clinical focus. 
After a survey of the current status and requirements in 6 different user groups (t0 survey), the intervention is carried out, followed by an evaluative t1 survey for before-after comparison. In other words, the intervention is a before-and-after comparison with regard to the user-friendliness of the guideline knowledge in the register.

The primary endpoint is usabilty (human level and technical level - interoperability and interconnectivity); other endpoints: acceptance of the (digital) guideline register, use of guideline content, assessment of the trustworthiness of guideline knowledge, facilitation of the application of the GRADE methodology. Import and export interfaces are also important.

The data is collected and analysed anonymously before and after via surveys and focus groups. In particular, the usability, acceptance and trustworthiness of the digital register and its content will be evaluated. In this way, further opportunities for improvement can be identified.
conditions: The study does not relate to individual diseases or health problems.

interventions.name:
The study is designed as a prospective, pre-post intervention study over a project time of three years with semi-quantitative (surveys) and qualitative (focus groups) methods.
